name: Madeira
note: Island of Madeira. Multiple candidates point to the same island with slight variations in geometry/focus. All three main candidates (a1715038, g2266877, s-2168434) represent the Madeira island itself.

name: Funchal
note: City of Funchal. Primary candidates n25255071 and i2052 correctly identify Funchal as a settlement in the municipality of Funchal. Multiple mentions across many regions confirm this is the main city.

name: Berlim
note: German city where medical and scientific works about Madeira were published in 1884, 1899, and 1906

name: Suíça
note: Country where Dr. Roland Krohn died in a sanatorium and where Dr. José de Almada studied

name: Selvagens
note: Selvagens Islands (archipelago). Candidates Q27088 and g2263082 both correctly identify the Selvagens archipelago, separate from Madeira proper but administratively part of Funchal municipality.

name: Cracóvia
note: Polish city where Kulczynski published work on arachnids from Madeira in 1899; also spelled Carcovia in the text

name: Terceira
note: Island in the Azores archipelago; mentioned in connection with the Order of Christ and as residence of poet Anastacio Moniz de Bettencourt

name: São Miguel
note: Largest island in the Azores; mentioned regarding oranges and the Câmara family

name: Porto Santo
note: Porto Santo is both an island and municipality with a single parish. Multiple candidates confirm this; a8435155 (Ilha do Porto Santo) is the island designation.

name: Piedade
matched_name: Igreja de Nossa Senhora da Piedade
note: Piedade in Porto Santo. The mention of Piedade in the context of Porto Santo and geological remains (maxilas found in calcareous bodies) points to Porto Santo. Igreja de Nossa Senhora da Piedade (a668358633) in Porto Santo parish is the best match for this location.

name: Desertas
note: Desertas Islands. Multiple candidates confirm the Desertas archipelago, distinct from Madeira proper. Located southeast of Madeira island, administratively part of Santa Cruz municipality.

name: Ponta Delgada
note: Ponta Delgada in Porto Santo. The encyclopedia specifically mentions 'Ponta Delgada, ao noroeste do Porto Santo' (northwest of Porto Santo). The candidate i2461 'Delgada' in Porto Santo parish is the correct location. Other Ponta Delgada candidates are in São Vicente (Madeira island), which is a different location.

name: Praia do Porto Santo
note: Beach/bay of Porto Santo. Multiple candidates specifically identify Praia do Porto Santo as a bay in Porto Santo parish. The encyclopedia extensively describes this beach, its characteristics, and activities there.

name: Ilhéu da Pontinha
note: Ilhéu (islet) in Funchal bay; historical cape; geonames candidate is most direct; OSM paths and street (Rua/Estrada da Pontinha) mark the location on land.

name: Fortaleza de São Tiago
note: Fort in Santa Maria Maior parish, Funchal; wikidata and OSM both identify it precisely; mentioned as limiting eastern edge of Funchal bay anchorage and located in Santa Maria Maior parish.

name: Escola Industrial do Funchal
note: Escola Industrial do Funchal (1892) is a lost building; no OSM candidate maps this specific institution; only general Funchal locations returned.

name: Lisboa
note: Portuguese capital where Henrique Franco de Sousa studied at the Academy of Fine Arts and where criminals were sentenced

name: Madrid
note: Spanish capital where Henrique Franco de Sousa visited scientific establishments and where João de Oliveira Sá Camelo Lampreia served in the legation

name: Paris
note: French capital where Henrique Franco de Sousa created artwork and where Visconde da Ribeira Brava lived; also where Dr. Juvenal Honório de Ornelas earned his medical degree

name: Dinamarca
note: Country in Northern Europe; Prince Frederick VII visited Madeira in 1846

name: Deserta Grande
note: Deserta Grande (Deserta) is the largest of three Desertas islands; OSM maps it accurately; encyclopedia places it in Desertas group; modern administrative location is Santa Cruz, Santa Cruz.

name: Capela de São João
note: Chapel in Ponta do Sol parish (Lombo de São João); article "Lombo de São João" states chapel is there; OSM maps Capela de São João in correct location; encyclopedia also mentions chapel in Ribeira Brava but the Ponta do Sol chapel is the named one with its own article.

name: Londres
note: Capital of England; mentioned for humid climate comparison and as publication location

name: Poiso
note: Sítio Poiso in Serra de Água parish, Arco da Calheta region; irig candidate is settlement; OSM paths confirm location.

name: Poiso
note: Poiso is a high-altitude locality (1390 m) mentioned across multiple regions: Camacha (Santa Cruz), Serra de Água (Ribeira Brava), São Vicente, and Seixal (Porto Moniz); candidates span these parishes; levada candidate in São Vicente indicates water infrastructure but not the settlement itself; returning multiple settlements as choices since encyclopedia references Poiso as a single known locality across the island's interior.

name: Pico do Areeiro
note: Pico do Arieiro (wikidata name spelling) = Pico do Areeiro (encyclopedia spelling); peak located in Curral das Freiras parish; irig building (Casa do Areeiro) in Monte marks settlement on approach route; miradouro candidate also marks viewpoint at peak location.

name: Paul da Serra
note: Paul da Serra is a high plateau spanning multiple parishes. The candidates include settlements named after it in Calheta and Ponta do Sol, and hiking routes crossing it. The Ovil (enclosure) in Ponta do Sol (a1467818221) marks the plateau area best; the plateau itself is not a mapped feature but this named area represents its location in the region mentioned most frequently in sources.

name: Fortaleza de São Lourenço
note: The Forte de São Lourenço (fort) in Sé, Funchal is the fortress mentioned in all sources, confirmed by multiple contemporary references to its location in the city center and its role as governor's residence and military installation.

name: Tenerife
note: Canary Island; notable windstorm in 1868 and visited by explorers

name: Orotava
note: Valley in Tenerife, Canary Islands; site of famous dragon tree destroyed in 1868 windstorm

name: Quinta Holloway
note: Quinta Holloway is mentioned only once as a location at 85 meters elevation where a humidity reading was taken in 1849. No candidates match this specific estate name. It was likely a private quinta in Funchal that is no longer mapped or has disappeared. Cannot determine precise parish from available information.

name: Itália
note: European country; mentioned for climate comparison and citrus crop pests

name: Palácio de São Lourenço
note: The Palácio de São Lourenço in Sé, Funchal is clearly identified as the governor's residence and official palace where state functions, banquets, and ceremonies were held. Multiple sources confirm its role and location in the city center.

name: Praça da Constituição
note: Praça da Constituição was an old square in Funchal, mentioned as 'ancient' by the 1920s, suggesting it was renamed or replaced. The Largo da Praça and Travessa da Praça in Sé parish may relate to it, but the sources indicate it was a distinct historical plaza that no longer bears that name. Located in the entry/waterfront area of Funchal, likely in Santa Maria Maior or Sé parish.

name: Club Funchalense
note: Club Funchalense was a social club that existed in the late 19th/early 20th century in Funchal where banquets and events were held. The club building itself is no longer mapped or has been repurposed. No current candidates directly match this historical institution.

name: Associação Comercial do Funchal
note: The Associação Comercial do Funchal (Commercial Association) in Sé is directly identified in Wikidata as the institution mentioned in the source, where Roberto Ivens traced his map of African exploration.

name: Jardim Municipal do Funchal
note: The Jardim Municipal do Funchal (Municipal Garden) in Sé is confirmed by multiple sources as the public garden in the city center, built on the site of the former Convent of São Francisco, with surrounding streets named after explorers Capelo and Ivens.

name: África
note: Continent; mentioned for exploration expeditions and penal deportation destinations

name: Marrocos
note: North African country; Portuguese military campaigns and knight exploits mentioned

name: Espanha
note: Iberian Peninsula country; Portuguese naval support during restoration period and military campaigns

name: Algarve
note: Region in southern Portugal; mentioned as origin of settlers to Madeira and as place where a captain-donatary arrived

name: Almeirim
note: Town in Portugal where João Gonçalves da Câmara died in 1580; mentioned in multiple contexts related to donatary succession

name: Vila Franca do Campo
note: Town in Azores where naval battle occurred on 23 July 1582 (also dated 26 July 1582 in another mention) involving D. Francisco de Portugal

name: Évora
note: City in Portugal where D. Luiz de Portugal, 4th Count of Vimioso, professed and died in a convent in 1637; also mentioned as a district

name: Lazareto de Gonçalo Aires
note: OSM node n4495548211 is tagged as 'Lazareto' building in Santa Maria Maior, matching the encyclopedia's mention of the lazareto at the mouth of Ribeira de Gonçalo Aires. The street 'Largo do Lazareto' and 'Rua do Lazareto' confirm the location. Although the stated parish is São Gonçalo, the actual site is in Santa Maria Maior where the river mouth meets the sea.

name: Igreja de Nossa Senhora da Graça (Estreito de Câmara de Lobos)
note: OSM multipolygon a296360200 'Nossa Senhora da Graça' church in Estreito de Câmara de Lobos matches the encyclopedia article about the church robbed in 1829. Multiple sources (j305, i2049) confirm this is the correct church.

name: Cais do Sodré
note: Wharf in Lisbon where criminals were executed in 1830

name: Levada
note: The text mentions a 'Levada' crossed by a procession from Nossa Senhora do Monte, but does not specify which of several levadas or settlements named 'Levada' in Funchal. Multiple candidates exist but none can be definitively matched to the specific channel mentioned in the context of processions from Monte. The reference is too vague.

name: Igreja de Nossa Senhora do Monte
note: OSM multipolygon a110395735 'Nossa Senhora do Monte' church in Monte parish matches all encyclopedia references. Multiple sources (j363, n927152528) confirm this is the correct church, the parish church where Emperor Charles of Austria was buried in 1922.

name: Ribeira dos Socorridos
note: The Ribeira dos Socorridos is a major stream forming a boundary between parishes (São Martinho/Santo António on left, Câmara de Lobos/Estreito de Câmara de Lobos on right). The OSM multilinestring features represent the stream across its full course from interior to sea. The reference to it serving as a divisor and its importance as a water source for levadas confirms this identification.

name: Pico Ruivo
note: Wikidata entry Q473169 'Pico Ruivo' peak in Faial, Santana matches the encyclopedia's geological description as part of the main crater formation and multiple expedition references to measuring this peak's height. OSM and geonames sources confirm this as Madeira's highest peak.

name: Lombo Gordo
note: Encyclopedia mentions 'Lombo Gordo, no Curral' in geological context as a formation at Paul da Serra. While 'Curral' refers to Curral das Freiras (Câmara de Lobos), the specific geological feature called Lombo Gordo is not distinctly mapped. The only candidate i947 'Lombo Gordo' is in Porto Moniz, not in Curral das Freiras area.

name: Bica da Cana
note: OSM node n337860996 'Bica da Cana' at Ponta do Sol matches the encyclopedia's detailed description of an experimental agricultural field created around 1914 on the Paul da Serra plateau. The building a319718158 'Casa de Abrigo da Bica de Cana' serves as proxy confirmation of the location.

name: Tem-te-não-caias
note: Stream Ribeira Tem-te Não Caias is the geological feature (basalt columns in valley). Multiple candidates exist; the stream feature best represents the location described in both geological articles about columnar basalt formations in this valley.

name: Lajinhas
note: The text explicitly states 'adro do Monte' (adro = church courtyard) and identifies a stone quarry site that gave the name to Lajinhas locality. OSM settlement at Monte matches perfectly; other Lajinha/Lapinha variants are in different regions (São Vicente, Santana, Santa Cruz).

name: Capela de São Luís
note: Chapel was located in Faial parish (Santana) near 'rua do Bispo' (old bishop street, now in Funchal), built 1725. The chapel no longer exists. Candidate a316553243 (Capela de São Luís de Tolosa) is in different parish (Sé, Funchal) and refers to different chapel. No surviving OSM feature identifies this lost chapel in Faial.

name: Cemitério das Angústias
note: OSM polygon matches the cemetery. Text mentions it was constructed 1838, located in São Pedro parish area but OSM places it in modern parish São Martinho (administrative boundary change). Multiple texts confirm this is the main Funchal cemetery for Catholics, distinct from S. Roque, Santa Luzia, and S. Gonçalo cemeteries.

name: Penha de Águia
note: Peak is the geological formation mentioned. OSM peak node n3414867404 at Faial, Santana is the exact feature. Multiple hiking routes follow the mountain (Vereda da Penha D'Aguia); levada also mapped. Mentions span multiple parishes but peak itself is at Faial/Santana. Wikidata alternative lists Porto da Cruz parish but OSM settlement and peak are clearly in Faial.

name: Torres
note: Text describes dikes between Torres and Torrinhas 'on route to Pico Ruivo' in central mountainous region. OSM peak Torres in Faial, Santana matches the geological formation of columnar dikes. Other Torres settlements (Curral das Freiras, Ponta do Sol) are in different regions not on central ridge route.

name: Achada do Ferreiro
note: Text locates this at 1522m altitude on route to Pico Ruivo in central mountain region. Several candidates exist (Pico Ferreiro in Ribeira Brava, Fenda do Ferreiro in Ribeira Brava, Palheiro Ferreiro in Funchal/Santa Cruz) but none specifically named 'Achada do Ferreiro'. Location is likely in Ribeira Brava municipality based on elevation and geography, but exact feature is not distinctly mapped as this name.

name: Cabo Girão
note: Cape/point feature clearly identified in multiple texts as major geographic landmark on south coast. OSM point at Câmara de Lobos matches stated location. Multiple related features exist (Fajãs do Cabo Girão, viewing platforms) but the cape itself is the main feature. Text notes debate about 'cabo' term for this cliff formation.

name: Ribeira de Machico
note: Stream in Machico mentioned in multiple contexts: near the mouth in Banda de Além fishing district, with lava channels, irrigation terraces, and as habitat for azevelho shrub. The OSM feature correctly identifies the main stream.

name: Fanal
note: Fanal is a locality in the mountains of Ribeira da Janela known for its lake, forest, and landscape. The PR13 hiking route (r2754724) and Lagoa do Fanal (a96116982) both mark the location. The settlement area spans Ribeira da Janela and Seixal parishes in OSM; encyclopedia places it in Ribeira da Janela.

name: Santo da Serra
note: Santo da Serra refers to the parish (modern: Santo António da Serra). The parish polygon (a8435149) is the exact match; the building (n970880024) marks the main settlement within it.

name: Santo da Serra
note: The encyclopedia mentions Santo da Serra as a parish with a lagoon and planalto in Monte/Porto Moniz region. This conflicts with the modern Santo António da Serra (Machico). OSM shows a parish boundary polygon (a8427679) for Santo António da Serra overlapping Santa Cruz municipality, suggesting administrative changes. Cannot determine precise historical location.

name: Santo da Serra
note: Santo da Serra mentioned across multiple regions as a parish and administrative location in Machico municipality. References include cheese factory (1895), experimental agricultural station, and administrative disputes. Modern parish name is Santo António da Serra (a8435149).

name: Ilhéu da Cal
note: Islet in Porto Santo with limestone quarries exploited for lime kilns. Wikidata entry Q1658454 correctly identifies this feature with alternative names.

name: Selvagem Grande
note: Island in the Selvagens archipelago known for limestone deposits and bird colonies. OSM polygon (a4862881) correctly identifies the main island.

name: Mornos
note: Locality in Porto Santo known for calcareous tufa formations and fossil shells. The irig_nd2 source (i2524) identifies Mornos as a settlement with shell deposits mentioned in geological context.

name: Capela da Misericórdia de Machico
matched_name: Santa Casa da Misericórdia de Machico
note: Santa Casa da Misericórdia de Machico is the institutional successor to the historical Capela da Misericórdia. The building/institution at this location matches the geographic reference in the text (at the mouth of the ribeira in Machico).

name: Ribeira de São João
note: Multiple segments of Ribeira de São João exist in different regions mentioned. The primary stream in Fajã da Ovelha (Calheta) is clearly identified. A second stream with same/variant names exists in Santo António (Funchal) mentioned in the Cortina da Cidade and Convento de São Francisco articles as the western boundary of old Funchal.

name: Pontinha
note: Pontinha settlement in Machico is the location referenced in Fajã da Ovelha article and Geologia article about the enseada (bay). The Cais da Pontinha in Funchal (i2106) is a different location but named after this place, mentioned in historical accounts of port construction.

name: Fajã dos Padres
note: Fajã dos Padres settlement is precisely located. The elevator and cable car are infrastructure associated with it; the beach area is part of the fajã.

name: Lugar de Baixo
note: Lugar de Baixo is clearly identified as a locality/sítio in Ponta do Sol. The lagoon and palacete are features within or named after this place.

name: Praia Formosa
note: Praia Formosa settlement marks the location of this coastal area in São Martinho. Multiple streets and infrastructure features in OSM confirm this as the recognized place name for this coastal locality.

name: Ponta da Oliveira
note: Ponta da Oliveira cape is precisely identified as a geographic feature marking the boundary between the two historic capitanias mentioned in the settlement and colonization article.

name: Ponta do Tristão
note: Ponta do Tristão is correctly identified as a cape in Porto Moniz. However, OSM places it in Porto Moniz parish rather than specifically Achadas da Cruz parish, though Achadas da Cruz is in Porto Moniz municipality. The geographic reference in texts clearly indicates the northern cape boundary.

name: Capela de São Sebastião
note: Strong match: OSM has Capela de São Sebastião in Ponta do Sol parish. The encyclopedia mentions it as pertaining to Câmara Municipal in the Vila article about Ponta do Sol. Texts also reference it as an early chapel in Funchal's history (Povoamento e Colonização, Nossa Senhora dos Valadouros, Jesuítas articles), but the Ponta do Sol chapel is the primary current location.

name: Igreja de Nossa Senhora do Calhau
note: The church was destroyed in the 1803 flood on the left bank of Ribeira de João Gomes near 'Poço do Calhau' in Funchal. No OSM record of the lost church exists. Candidates like 'O Calhau' building and various Calhau-named features in other parishes do not represent this specific destroyed church. The historical location in Santa Maria Maior parish is known but the structure no longer exists.

name: Ribeira de João Gomes
note: Perfect match: OSM has the Ribeira de João Gomes stream mapped as a MultiLineString in Santa Maria Maior. The encyclopedia extensively references it as the major watercourse in Funchal where key historical events occurred (1438 church founding, 1803 flood, fortifications). Multiple text sections confirm its location and importance.

name: Sé do Funchal
note: Excellent match: OSM feature a110317488 is Sé do Funchal cathedral in Sé parish, Funchal. The encyclopedia mentions it extensively as the cathedral seat, location of episcopal palace, venue for processions and religious ceremonies. This is definitively the correct location.

name: Igreja de Santa Maria Maior
note: Perfect match: OSM has Igreja de Santa Maria Maior (also known as Igreja do Socorro or Igreja de Santiago Menor) in Santa Maria Maior parish. The encyclopedia describes it as the parish church (sede da paróquia) where important processions arrived from the Sé and where the feast of Santiago Menor was celebrated.

name: Igreja do Colégio
note: Excellent match: Wikidata Q10300764 identifies Igreja de São João Evangelista also known as Igreja do Colégio (Jesuit College Church) in São Pedro parish. The encyclopedia references it as the Igreja do Colégio where various religious events occurred (assassin refuge, Nossa Senhora da Luz festival, Procissão da Cinza). Location in São Pedro aligns with text descriptions.

name: Torre do Tombo
note: National archive in Lisbon where historical documents related to Madeira are stored

name: Fortaleza de São João Baptista do Pico
Pico do Castelo
note: Strong match: OSM has Pico Castelo (peak) in Porto Santo parish, Porto Santo island. Encyclopedia describes it as a refuge for Porto Santo inhabitants from pirates, a military stronghold during Spanish rule, and source of water runoff affecting Funchal enclosures. Multiple articles confirm this location.

name: Rabaçal
note: Good match: Multiple OSM features mark Rabaçal as a building/locality in Calheta parish. Encyclopedia describes it as a picturesque highland place at 1000m altitude, 15km from Calheta village, connected by good road, with waterfalls (Vinte e Cinco Fontes) and various levadas. Though encyclopedia states parish 'Ribeira da Janela', current OSM places it in Calheta municipality.

name: Alfândega do Funchal
note: Two sources identify the same building: irig_nd1 (j632) and Wikidata (Q76955048). Mentions confirm location in Sé, Funchal with details about the building itself.

name: Pernambuco
note: Region in Brazil; Madeira was required to contribute resources for its restoration in 1637; associated with João Fernandes Vieira

name: Tomar
note: Town in Portugal where Cortes were to be held in May 1619 for swearing in Prince D. Filipe; headquarters of the Order of Christ's vicar

name: Porto
note: Major Portuguese city mentioned in context of 1820 revolution and population density comparisons

name: Portalegre
note: Portuguese city and district mentioned in electoral and population contexts

name: Largo da Sé
note: Wikidata source explicitly names 'Largo da Sé' with historical aliases matching encyclopedia text. Rua da Sé is adjacent/same location complex.

name: Convento da Encarnação
matched_name: Mosteiro de Nossa Senhora da Encarnação do Funchal
note: Mosteiro de Nossa Senhora da Encarnação (OSM a453303712) and Igreja da Encarnação (j425) are the same complex in Santa Luzia. Mentions confirm location as convent that housed seminary.

name: Convento de Santa Clara
note: OSM node n300363360 explicitly named 'Convento de Santa Clara' in São Pedro. Multiple mentions confirm this location hosted nuns and served various functions.

name: Louros
note: Encyclopedia states São Gonçalo but OSM places Louros in Santa Maria Maior (modern boundary). Mentions describe experimental agricultural fields and Junta Agrícola facilities matching this location. Multiple confirming references to this sítio.

name: Capela dos Santos Reis
note: Single mention places chapel 'proximo do hospital' (near hospital) in context of misericórdia. Lost building with no OSM match. Located in Funchal but parish unclear; mentions suggest near Hospital de Santa Isabel area (Sé/Santa Maria Maior region).

name: Sanatório dos Marmeleiros
note: OSM n1768511496 is 'Marmeleiros' building in Monte. Estrada dos Marmeleiros (w24992232 etc.) follows the same area. Datas Históricas confirms 1905 foundation in Monte district.

name: Hospital de Santa Isabel
note: Wikidata Q112123472 identifies 'Hospital de Santa Isabel' in Sé. Encyclopedia mentions multiple locations: originally near Rua do Hospital Velho (Santa Maria Maior), then moved. Rua de Santa Isabel (w111497951) in Santa Maria Maior marks former location. Current identification in Sé is approximate.

name: Capela de São Luís de Tolosa
matched_name: Capela de São Luís de Tolosa

name: Rua do Mosteiro Novo
note: The Mosteiro Novo building is the primary feature; the Rua do Mosteiro Novo street is named after it and runs through the same location in Sé parish, Funchal.

name: Largo do Ribeiro Real
note: OSM has 'Largo Visconde do Ribeiro Real' in Sé, matching the encyclopedia's Largo do Ribeiro Real where the Episcopal Palace was located. The mention of proximity to British cemetery and other details confirm Funchal's old center location.

name: Japão
note: Origin of camphora tree, magnolia, and bamboo plants mentioned in the encyclopedia

name: América tropical
note: Region of origin for avocado tree (Persea gratíssima) cultivated in Madeira

name: Beja
note: Portuguese city and district, mentioned for population density and convent connections

name: Bragança
note: Portuguese city and district, administrative positions held by Madeirans

name: Castelo Branco
note: Portuguese city and district mentioned in population density and electoral contexts

name: Braga
note: Portuguese city with archbishopric; mentioned for population density and administrative appointments

name: Levada dos Piornais
note: The Levada dos Piornais route (r4745248) is the main channel. Supporting proxy features include the Vereda, Rua, Rampa, and Travessa dos Piornais which follow or mark the levada's path in São Martinho.

name: Levadas do Rabaçal
note: The encyclopedia mentions two levadas: 'Levada Velha do Rabaçal' (r19282964: PR 6.4) and 'Levada Nova do Rabaçal' (Q10317702: also known as Levada das 25 Fontes). Both are in Calheta. The construction date of 1835 and location context confirm these are the correct channels, though they split into three branches each.

name: Levada de Santa Luzia
note: The hiking routes r18452500 and r18452558 (026: Centro ↔ Levada de Santa Luzia) represent the levada. The stream r6391731 (Ribeira de Santa Luzia) feeds the levada. The mentions span multiple parishes (Santa Luzia, Caniço, Monte, Ponta do Sol) showing the levada's long course; Rua de Santa Luzia marks its path through the city.

name: Levada das Hortas
note: No specific levada feature is mapped in OSM with this name. Rua das Hortas in Santa Luzia parish serves as a proxy, marking the location associated with the historical levada. The encyclopedia mentions it alongside Santa Luzia and Bom Sucesso levadas in Funchal.

name: Ribeira de Santa Luzia
note: The Ribeira de Santa Luzia stream is mapped in OSM (r6391731) in Monte parish. The encyclopedia describes it as one of three rivers crossing the city Funchal, flowing from higher elevations and supporting multiple levadas in its basin.

name: Levada de D. Isabel
matched_name: Levada do Lombo de Dona Isabel
note: The encyclopedia calls it 'Levada de D. Isabel' (also 'Levada da Fundoa'), serving São Roque, São Pedro, and Santa Luzia. OSM has 'Levada do Lombo de Dona Isabel' (r19612971) in Santo António, which is named after the same person but in a different location. No exact match found for the original levada; parish and municipality are stated as São Roque, Funchal.

name: Levada dos Moinhos
note: Levada dos Moinhos in Funchal (Santa Maria Maior region) matches the primary candidate. The mentions also reference this levada irrigating Fajã da Ovelha and Estreito da Calheta (Calheta), which may involve separate sections of the same channel. The candidate w685424456/w1125278639 in São Pedro represents the main mapped levada. The stream Ribeira dos Moinhos in Estreito da Calheta (i2779) and Ponta do Pargo (w905626186) are tributaries/sources, not the levada itself. Streets and paths in Estreito da Calheta (w132836871, w111871367) mark the levada's proximity but are not the levada.

name: Ribeira de Câmara de Lobos
note: The mention in 'Levadas' article from Santa Maria Maior (Funchal) references 'ribeiras de Machico e de Câmara de Lobos' as historical irrigation points at coastal margins. No OSM candidate explicitly represents a river/stream named 'Ribeira de Câmara de Lobos'. Candidates are related features (ETAR, promenade, municipality boundary) but not the stream itself. The reference is too vague to map to a specific watercourse.

name: Levada do Coquim
note: The Levada do Coquim was being constructed to irrigate Boaventura and Ponta Delgada (northern parishes, likely São Vicente municipality). No OSM candidate matches this name. Generic levada candidates are too distant. The construction was initiated ~50 years before 1921 (1870s) with questionable success. Cannot determine exact location from available data.

name: Levada do Rabaçal
note: The Levada do Rabaçal is extensively documented across multiple regions (Fajã da Ovelha, Arco da Calheta, Estreito da Calheta, Prazeres, Ponta do Pargo in Calheta municipality). The primary mapped candidates are r19282964 (Levada Velha do Rabaçal) and Q10317702 (Levada das 25 Fontes/Levada Nova do Rabaçal), both in Calheta parish, representing sections of this major state levada. The Túnel do Rabaçal (w39503521) and associated infrastructure (Casa Rabaçal, visitor center) confirm location.

name: Levada da Serra do Faial
note: The Levada da Serra do Faial is the most extensive state levada after Rabaçal, originating in Serra do Faial (Santana) and flowing across multiple parishes. Multiple OSM candidates represent different sections: r1354532 (Camacha, Santa Cruz), r19612952 (Porto da Cruz, Machico - marked as part of Levada do Furado/Serra do Faial), r19612953, r19612955 (São Roque do Faial/Faial, Santana), r19613358 (Levada da Faja da Nogueira, Faial, Santana). All are part of the same system. Mentions confirm routes through Lamaceiros and Porto da Cruz.

name: Levada do Furado
note: The Levada do Furado originates at Ribeiro Frio (Faial parish, Santana) and flows to Porto da Cruz. Primary candidate r2754660 (PR 10, Porto da Cruz, Machico) is the main hiking route along the levada. The old section w222697753+ (Levada do Furado Velho, Prazeres, Calheta) represents an older branch serving western parishes. Both are part of the same levada system with different irrigation routes.

name: Levada do Juncal
note: The Levada do Juncal flows from sources in the north (São Roque do Faial/Santana) and carries water to eastern parishes including Água de Pena (Machico). Primary candidates r19612951 (Levada do Juncal) and r19612954 (Levada Nova do Juncal) represent the main channel in São Roque do Faial. Mentions confirm mirantes (viewpoints) along the levada and connection to the combined Lamaceiros aqueduct with Levada da Serra do Faial.

name: Levada do Curral e Castelejo
note: The Levada do Curral e Castelejo is explicitly stated as a private levada in Funchal council, specifically in Santo António parish. Primary candidates i2835 (Levada do Curral e Castelejo, irig_nd2) and r4444577 (Levada do Curral, OSM) both map this feature. The related i2836 (Levada Nova do Curral e Castelejo) represents a newer section. Estrada Levada do Curral e Castelejo (w110441024+) is the road along the levada.

name: Estrebarias
matched_name: Túnel das Estrebarias (Levada do Furado Velho)
note: The text mentions Estrebarias as a peak (Pico) in the context of a levada route from Funchal's Santa Maria Maior toward Calheta. The OSM candidate is a tunnel/path (Túnel das Estrebarias) on the Levada do Furado Velho in Estreito da Calheta, which matches the geographic region and context of a feature along a levada system. While not the peak itself, this named feature marks the location.

name: Serra do Faial
note: Serra do Faial is mentioned in multiple contexts: as a location in Faial (Santana) where a forest nursery was established ('Passada da Novilha'), and as a state-owned levada system. However, the candidates provided are mostly buildings, facilities, or road routes in or near Faial, not the Serra (plateau/mountain range) itself. No direct OSM mapping of the Serra do Faial plateau exists in the candidates. The correct parish is Faial, Santana.

name: Juncal
note: The encyclopedia mentions 'levada do Juncal' as one of the state-owned levadas. OSM has 'Levada do Juncal' (r19612951) explicitly mapped as a levada in São Roque do Faial, Santana, which matches the context perfectly.

name: Serra de São Jorge
note: The text mentions Serra de São Jorge as a plateau/serra, partly state-owned ('Baldios' article) and with a state-owned levada system ('Levadas' article). The candidates are mostly buildings, facilities, and road routes in or near São Jorge, but no direct mapping of the Serra (plateau) itself. The parish is São Jorge, Santana.

name: Ribeira do Inferno
note: The encyclopedia's 'Ribeira do Inferno' article confirms this is a stream in São Vicente parish that separates São Vicente from Seixal. OSM maps this as 'Ribeira do Inferno' (MultiLineString across multiple ways) in the Seixal/Porto Moniz area. The article also mentions the Levada da Ribeira do Inferno (r19612805) which exists in OSM in São Vicente, showing the stream has both a channel and an associated levada. The main stream choices are the west/Seixal section.

name: Monte Medonho
note: The encyclopedia identifies Monte Medonho as a location in São Vicente parish where the Levada do Monte Medonho originates. OSM has this levada explicitly mapped (Levada do Monte Medonho, w398260981 and related ways) in São Vicente. While the peak/sítio itself may not be separately mapped, the levada bearing its name is the authoritative geographic reference.

name: Furado
matched_name: Chão das Feiteiras - Pico do Suna - Levada do Furado - Chão das Feiteiras
note: The text mentions 'levada do Furado' as one of the state-owned levadas. OSM has a hiking route 'Chão das Feiteiras - Pico do Suna - Levada do Furado - Chão das Feiteiras' (r19608179) explicitly named after this levada in Porto da Cruz, Machico. This marks the location of the levada system referenced in the encyclopedia.

name: Prazeres
note: The encyclopedia identifies Prazeres as an old sítio (locality) in Monte parish, Funchal, where a chapel of Nossa Senhora dos Prazeres once stood, approximately at the location of Monte Palace Hotel. The OSM candidates for 'Prazeres' are all in Prazeres parish, Calheta (a different municipality), not in Monte, Funchal. No suitable candidate exists in the correct parish. The place is lost or not mapped in its original Monte location.

name: Cumeada
note: The mention describes a levada project from the 1830s routing water to fields called 'Cumiada' and then to parishes including Canhas, Arco da Calheta, Estreito, Prazeres, Fajã da Ovelha, Ponta do Pargo, and Porto do Moniz. The candidates Encumeada are buildings in different municipalities (São Vicente and Ribeira Brava) unrelated to this water distribution context. No reliable candidate matches the sítio Cumeada in the levada route described.

name: Rossada
note: The mention places Rossada on the Levada do Rabaçal between Ribeira da Janela and other points along a described channel. Candidates Ossada (Faial, Santana) and Roçada (Caniçal, Machico and Boa Ventura, São Vicente) are in different regions from the Rabaçal area and do not match the context of this levada channel.

name: Ligarte
note: Ligarte is described as a point on the Levada do Rabaçal in a specific section with measured braças distances between Rossada and Pico Gordo. The only candidate 'Gate' (a fort in Monte, Funchal) does not match this levada geography. No suitable candidate found.

name: Pico Gordo
note: Pico Gordo is mentioned in the Levada do Rabaçal article as a peak along the channel route, positioned between Ligarte and Pico do Cotum. The settlement Pico Gordo in Calheta parish matches this geographical context. A second mention in the Bartolomeu article describes it as one of two peaks where the Ribeira (Bartolomeu) originates, consistent with this location.

name: Lombo da Aveira
note: Lombo da Aveira is mentioned as a ridge/location on the Levada do Rabaçal between Pico Gordo and Pico do Cotum. Candidates 'Lombo da Eira' (São Vicente) and 'Eira do Lombo' (Funchal) are in wrong parishes/municipalities and do not fit the levada route context described.

name: Pico do Cotum
note: Pico do Cotum is described as a peak on the Levada do Rabaçal, positioned after Lombo da Aveira and before the route branches toward Calheta via Estrebarias. The many candidates named 'Pico' or variations are scattered across Madeira and none specifically matches 'Cotum' in the levada geography context.

name: Vinte e Cinco Fontes
note: Vinte e Cinco Fontes is described as a scenic location near Rabaçal with multiple springs cascading from cliffs, feeding the Levada Nova do Rabaçal. The Levada das 25 Fontes (w1429803960) is the channel itself in Calheta, and the Madre da Levada springs (n2173880432) mark the source area in Ribeira da Janela, Porto Moniz. Both are part of the same system. The location is approximately 3 km from Rabaçal houses in the Calheta area.

name: Fonte do Cedro
note: Fonte do Cedro (spring of the cedar) feeds the Levada Nova do Rabaçal alongside Vinte e Cinco Fontes. Candidates include various Cedro-related locations but none specifically identifies a spring called 'Fonte do Cedro'. The context places it in the Rabaçal water system (Calheta area). No exact mapping found; precision limited to the municipality where the levada system is located.

name: Lombo da Raiz
note: Two candidates at same location (one in Porto da Cruz, one without parish data): both are the Lombo da Raiz where levadas separate. The encyclopedia mentions it in Santo da Serra context but OSM places it at the boundary or in adjacent parishes. Both n6256735045 and i1289 mark the same feature where levadas split.

name: Choupana
note: Settlement Choupana in Santa Maria Maior, Funchal, well-attested in text as locality where levadas run and quintas are located.

name: Ribeira da Laje
note: Ribeira das Lajes (plural in OSM) corresponds to Ribeira da Laje (singular in text). Multiple way segments form one stream in Faial parish where levada encabeza according to article.

name: Pico do Infante
note: Encyclopedia states Pico do Infante in Camacha (Santa Cruz), but OSM peak is in São Gonçalo (Funchal) at boundary. Street 'Caminho do Pico do Infante' in Camacha may better represent the parish location mentioned, though peak itself is in São Gonçalo.

name: Pico do Infante
note: Peak in São Gonçalo, Funchal where levada sources converge and panorama views extend from Terreiro da Luta.

name: Levada dos Accionistas
note: Levada particular branching from Juncal/Furado aqueducts toward Santa Cruz. No OSM feature specifically named 'Levada dos Accionistas'. Generic levada features exist but cannot be matched to this specific channel without more precise routing data.

name: Caminho do Meio
note: Road in Santa Maria Maior where levada terminates and chapel of Nossa Senhora do Bom Sucesso is located. Well-mapped in OSM.

name: Ribeiro Frio
note: Settlement Ribeiro Frio at 750m altitude, junction point for levadas and major crossroads on road to Santana. Multiple supporting features (fontanário, trout house, forest park) confirm location.

name: Lamaceiros
note: Settlement in Porto Moniz. Multiple mentions confirm it is a sítio in Porto Moniz with a chapel of São Pedro. OSM node n1742394940 (Lamaçeiros, settlement) matches the stated location exactly.

name: Lamaceiros
note: Sítio in Santo da Serra (Santo António da Serra), Machico. The encyclopedia article describes it as a picturesque site with views over Porto da Cruz, Faial and Santana parishes, 3km from the parish church. Two OSM settlement nodes in the correct parish are provided (coordinates differ slightly but both in Santo António da Serra).

name: Ribeira do Juncal
note: Stream (Ribeira do Juncal) where the Levada do Juncal originates. The text mentions it in the context of levadas flowing toward Lamaceiros in Machico/Santana region. OSM stream features in Porto da Cruz, Machico match.

name: Levada da Serra de São Jorge
note: Levada serving São Jorge, Santana and Faial parishes with origin at Pé dos Poios in the Serra de São Jorge. Multiple OSM candidates are hiking routes (HF 103, HF 138) not the levada itself. The levada infrastructure is not directly mapped in OSM; only roads/routes through the area exist.

name: Pé dos Poios
note: Source location (sítio) in the serra of São Jorge where Levada da Serra de São Jorge originates. OSM node n1511590885 (Pé do Pico, building in São Jorge) is nearby but Pé dos Poios itself is not mapped; used as proxy for the general location.

name: Levada da Fajã dos Vinháticos
note: Levada built 1860-1904, replaced by Levada da Serra de São Jorge in 1904. OSM relation r19612822 (Levada da Faja dos Vinhaticos) in Serra de Água, Ribeira Brava matches the historical levada.

name: Ilha
note: Sítio della parish of São Jorge (now formally Ilha parish in Santana). The encyclopedia describes it as surrounded by bifurcating ribeira, a morgadio established 1559. OSM settlement node n1832777810 (Ilha, settlement in Ilha parish, Santana) is the exact match.

name: Levada do Monte Medonho
note: Levada originating at Monte Medonho in Serra de São Vicente, irrigating Ribeira Brava and Tábua since 1908 (previously São Vicente). OSM linestring features w398260981, w625897394, w625897393 (Levada do Monte Medonho) in São Vicente parish match exactly.

name: Levada da Ribeira do Inferno
note: OSM has Levada da Ribeira do Inferno (r19612805) in São Vicente parish, matching the encyclopedia's description: originates in Ribeira do Inferno and irrigates São Vicente parish. The mentions confirm the levada supplies São Vicente and originates from the Ribeira do Inferno stream.

name: Terreiro das Galinhas
note: The encyclopedia places Terreiro das Galinhas as a high mountain (serrania) two leagues from Funchal city, with water sources that feed the Levada de Santa Luzia. OSM has no exact match for this mountain peak. Candidates like Terreiro (settlement in São Vicente), Fajã das Galinhas (Câmara de Lobos), and others are in wrong locations or wrong types. The feature appears to be a lost or unidentified peak in the upper watershed above Funchal.

name: Tornos
note: The Tornos is a spring/water source in Monte parish. OSM has Aguas dos Tornos (r19639799, stream) and Nascente de Tornos Altos (i2642, cliff spring source) both in Monte, Funchal. Multiple mentions confirm these are the abundant springs that feed the Levada de Santa Luzia and other levadas, located above the Ribeira de Santa Luzia in the Montado do Barreiro area.

name: Socorro
note: The encyclopedia mentions Socorro as a sítio in parish Canhas (in Ponta do Sol municipality, not Funchal as stated—this is an error in the encyclopedia). OSM has Socorro settlement in Canhas, Ponta do Sol (n3995321380). The mention of a chapel and school in Socorro in Canhas confirms this location. A second Socorro exists in Santa Maria Maior, Funchal, but that is a different place.

name: Fundoa de Cima
note: Fundoa is a sítio in São Roque parish where the Levada de Dona Isabel has its embocadura (outlet), mentioned in the 1866 levada measurements. OSM has Fundoa settlement (n1824172987) in São Roque, Funchal, and several related way nodes (Fundoa Cima D, S2A, S1A) marking infrastructure at this location.

name: Ribeira das Cales
note: Ribeira das Cales is mentioned as a major stream in Funchal where levada waters divide and where Roberto Page built a refuge house. OSM maps it as a stream (w198949181, w1340122472, w1340122473) in Monte parish, Funchal. The mentions confirm it receives water from the upper levadas near Fundoa and feeds into Ribeira de João Gomes.

name: São Pedro
note: The encyclopedia lists São Pedro as a principal sítio in São Jorge parish. OSM has São Jorge (S. Pedro) (i2605), a settlement in São Jorge, Santana. The Capela de São Pedro (n1493432017) is also located here, confirming the site.

name: Levada do Castelejo
note: The encyclopedia mentions Levada do Castelejo as a 16th-century levada. OSM has Levada do Castelejo (r5562195, r19613324) in Porto da Cruz parish, Machico municipality. However, the mentions refer to it irrigating São Martinho and São Pedro in Funchal, suggesting a different channel. OSM also has Levada do Curral e Castelejo (i2835, i2836) in Santo António, Funchal, which may be the Funchal channel, but the primary OSM Castelejo levada is in Machico. The channel likely extends across multiple municipalities.

name: Fajã dos Chiqueiros
note: The text mentions 'Fajã dos Chiqueiros' in Curral das Freiras parish, Câmara de Lobos municipality, where the Levada dos Piornais originates near Ribeira do Cidrão and Ribeira do Gato. Candidate n13567887301 'Fajã' in Câmara de Lobos parish is the closest match in the correct municipality, though the specific 'Chiqueiros' location is not precisely mapped.

name: Levada Nova de Câmara de Lobos
note: The text describes the Levada Nova de Câmara de Lobos dividing water at Fajã do Poio in Santo António parish, Funchal. The levada itself is not directly mapped, but 'Rua Nova da Praia' in Câmara de Lobos municipality serves as a proxy for the location reference.

name: Lourais
note: The text mentions 'montado dos Lourais' in the context of levada improvements in Santa Maria Maior (the region where the article is located). Candidate n3995321070 'Louros' in Santa Maria Maior, Funchal matches exactly in the correct parish and municipality.

name: Cales
note: The text mentions 'sítio das Calles' as the location of a water distribution box for Levada dos Moinhos and Levada de Santa Luzia. Candidate r19613344 'Levada das Cales' in Monte parish, Funchal is the correct levada feature in the right location.

name: Ribeira do Seixal
note: The text lists Ribeira do Seixal as one of the major streams originating in the high mountains. The candidates are the stream segments in Seixal parish, Porto Moniz municipality, which match exactly.

name: Ribeira de São Vicente
note: Multiple texts confirm this stream originates in Encumeada and flows through São Vicente parish. Candidate i3057 'Ribeira de S. Vicente' in São Vicente parish and municipality matches exactly.

name: Ribeira da Ponta do Sol
note: Multiple texts confirm this stream flows through Ponta do Sol parish and municipality. The candidates are the stream segments mapping this river exactly.

name: Ribeira da Madalena
note: The text confirms this stream desembarks in Madalena do Mar parish, Ponta do Sol municipality. The candidates are the stream segments that map this river exactly in the correct location.

name: Levada do Pico da Urze
note: OSM relation r19612842 is the Levada do Pico da Urze in Calheta, matching the encyclopedia's description of this levada supplying the Arco da Calheta with abundant water from ~1,350m altitude.

name: Levada do Caramujo
matched_name: Levada da Serra da Ponta de Pargo inf
note: The encyclopedia describes this levada as having origin in Ribeira do Inferno at the base of Pico Ruivo do Paul at 1,185m, supplying São Vicente. OSM ways w214419121 and w385356693 form the Levada in São Vicente parish, matching the stated municipality and function.

name: Campo Grande
note: The encyclopedia locates Campo Grande on the Paul da Serra plateau where experimental water retention works were conducted, and describes it as an inhospitable point. OSM settlement i2369 in Calheta matches this location on the plateau.

name: Ribeiro do Alecrim
note: The encyclopedia describes waters flowing through Ribeiro do Alecrim to Ribeira da Janela from the Paul da Serra plateau. OSM way Ribeira do Alecrim in Calheta matches this stream draining the plateau region.

name: Chão das Mesas
note: The encyclopedia mentions Chão das Mesas as a location on the plateau suitable for dam construction, alongside Ariais or Campo Pequeno. OSM point Mesas (n3995321096) in Camacha represents this settlement; Chão das Mesas likely refers to the area around Mesas on the Paul da Serra plateau.

name: Campo Pequeno
note: The encyclopedia identifies Campo Pequeno (also called Ariais) on the Paul da Serra plateau as a site for potential water diversion from Ribeiro do Lagedo. OSM settlement Campo Pequeno in Calheta matches this location.

name: Ribeiro do Lajedo
note: The encyclopedia names this stream 'Ribeiro do Lagedo' flowing from the Paul da Serra to Ribeira da Janela. OSM features w164953189, w693641402, w693641403 form the Ribeira do Lajeado in Calheta; variant spelling of Lajedo/Lagedo is consistent with Portuguese orthographic variation.

name: Camacha
note: The encyclopedia lists Camacha among the principal sítios of Porto Santo parish and mentions it as one of the sandy terrain locations for water infiltration in the island's water distribution system. OSM settlement n1573920835 confirms Camacha in Porto Santo parish on Porto Santo island.

name: Eira Velha
note: Sitio da Eira Velha in Porto Santo matches the locality mentioned in the Levadas article as an infiltration site in Porto Santo's water distribution system.

name: Areias
note: Areias is a documented sítio in Porto Santo parish, mentioned as one of the main localities and as an infiltration area for water distribution. The OSM area feature matches the geographic entity.

name: Levada Velha do Rabaçal
note: PR 6.4 - Levada Velha do Rabaçal is the hiking route that follows the levada. The encyclopedia mentions it originates at Fontes do Risco with specific measurements (24,000m extension, 450m Furado Velho tunnel, 65 l/s flow).

name: Fontes do Risco
note: Risco waterfall in Calheta represents the springs (Fontes do Risco) at 1045m altitude that are the source of Levada Velha do Rabaçal. The waterfall marks the location of these water sources.

name: Levada Nova do Rabaçal
note: Levada Nova in Calheta originates in Ribeira dos Cedros at 990m altitude. Multiple OSM way segments form this levada system. The encyclopedia mentions it has 800m Furado Novo tunnel and receives water from Vinte e Cinco Fontes and Ribeira Grande tributaries.

name: Ribeira dos Cedros
note: Ribeira dos Cedros stream in Calheta is documented in irig_nd2 as the source of Levada Nova do Rabaçal at 990m altitude. Located in the Fajã da Ovelha region as mentioned in the encyclopedia.

name: Pico Ruivo do Paul
note: Ruivo do Paul peak in Calheta at 1185m altitude is the base of Ribeira do Inferno where Levada do Caramujo originates. The OSM name 'Ruivo do Paul' is a variant of 'Pico Ruivo do Paul' with identical location.

name: Levada do Lombo do Moiro
note: Levada do Lombo do Mouro in Ribeira Brava matches the encyclopedia's 'Levada do Lombo do Moiro' (mouro/moiro spelling variant). Originates from Ribeiras do Folhadal, Pináculo and Monte Trigo at 1450m with 10,600m extension and 18 l/s flow.

name: Caldeirão do Inferno
note: Mentioned as origin of Levada da Serra de São Jorge at 920m altitude in the Serra de São Jorge. OSM candidates n5894060410 and i1407 both map Caldeirão do Inferno in São Jorge/Santana, with i1407 being the more specific location at Ilha parish. The madre (source point) n6556476425 is also present.

name: Caldeirão Verde
note: Multiple mentions place Caldeirão Verde in Santana parish as a scenic sítio. OSM settlement n5894060253 and levada route r2235099 both map this location at Ilha/Santana. The Levada do Caldeirão Verde (r2235099) directly corresponds to the water channel mentioned.

name: Caldeirão Verde
note: Queimadas article specifically places Caldeirão Verde in São Jorge parish. Wikidata Q63378596 directly maps the building at São Jorge/Santana. The hiking route r4441701 (PR 9 - Levada do Caldeirão Verde) follows the channel but is classified as Ilha parish in OSM; used as proxy.

name: Ribeira Seca
note: Multiple sources confirm Ribeira Seca as a stream in Machico parish, origin of Levada da Serra do Faial at 1100m. OSM i2797 is the stream itself. Streets w385511538 and w26415360 (Caminho da Ribeira Seca, Estrada da Ribeira Seca) are proxies for the stream location.

name: Serralhal
note: Water source in Caniço parish mentioned in Levadas article as potable source generating annual revenue. OSM n5032654163 maps Serralhal settlement in Caniço/Santa Cruz, serving as proxy for the spring location.

name: Serra de Água
note: Listed as a principal sítio of Seixal parish. OSM n13763159901 'Serra d'Água' maps the settlement in Seixal/Porto Moniz with slight spelling variation (d'Água vs de Água), which is a common orthographic variant for the period.

name: Ponta Delgada
note: City in the Azores islands, mentioned as seat of customs authority and location of publication

name: Angra do Heroísmo
note: City in the Azores islands, mentioned in context of customs and publications

name: Piornais
note: Multiple sources confirm Piornais in São Martinho, Funchal, as a sítio and location of morgado and chapel of Nossa Senhora da Ajuda. OSM n3995321209 and i603 both map the settlement. Levada dos Piornais (r4745248) is also present.

name: Castelejo
matched_name: Levada Nova do Curral e Castelejo
note: Mentioned in 1562 royal charter regarding levada. Multiple levadas named Castelejo exist. The i2835/i2836 entries (Levada do Curral e Castelejo and Levada Nova do Curral e Castelejo) in Santo António/Funchal are the most likely 16th-century references. r5562195 and r19613324 in Porto da Cruz/Machico are alternative Castelejo levadas.

name: Igreja de Nossa Senhora da Piedade (Canhas)
matched_name: Igreja de Nossa Senhora da Piedade
note: Igreja de Nossa Senhora da Piedade is the exact match in Canhas, Ponta do Sol. The text mentions this church as a stop in the May processions. Candidate j252 is the church itself in the correct parish.

name: Lombada
note: The text from Gaspar Frutuoso describes a large property (fazenda) near Magdalena in Arco da Calheta with sugar mill and sugarcane fields. Lombada do Loreto (n3995321001) is the settlement in Arco da Calheta that matches this location. Other Lombadas are in different parishes.

name: Lombada
note: The text specifically states the viveiro (plant nursery) for northern species was situated in Lombada, in the parish of Monte. Quinta da Lombada (a433805096) in Monte matches this description. CAM Lombada (n13522404955) is also in Monte but is a modern facility, while the quinta represents the historical location better.

name: Capela de São Sebastião (Ponta do Sol)
note: The text describes a 1600 document stating the third day of Ladainhas processions went to the chapel of São Sebastião in the town/vila (Ponta do Sol). Candidate a469517934 is Capela de São Sebastião in Ponta do Sol parish, exactly matching the location.

name: Capela de Nossa Senhora do Livramento (Lombo das Adegas)
matched_name: Capela de Nossa Senhora do Livramento
note: The text explicitly places this chapel in Lombo das Adegas in Ponta do Sol. Candidate j274 is Capela de Nossa Senhora do Livramento in Ponta do Sol parish, the exact match. The OSM building n14167507302 confirms the location.

name: Capela de Santo Amaro (Lombada)
note: Two mentions place this chapel in Lombada, Ponta do Sol: one describes it as ruins attributed to João Esmeraldo, the other mentions it as a stop in Via Sacra processions. Candidate a1108209766 is Capela de Santo Amaro in Ponta do Sol's Lombada area, the exact match.

name: Caminho da Lombada
note: The text mentions a 'Caminho da Lombada' in Ponta do Sol where the Furna do Calvário was located as a station of Via Sacra processions. The candidate 'Caminho do Tornadouro da Lombada' in Ponta do Sol is the best match, being in the correct parish and referring to the same path network around Lombada.

name: Furna do Calvário
note: The text locates the Furna do Calvário on Caminho da Lombada in Ponta do Sol as a station of Via Sacra processions. No OSM candidate specifically represents this cave/shelter. While Calvário settlements exist in other parishes, the context clearly indicates Ponta do Sol. The specific furna feature is not mapped in OSM.

name: Cândia
note: Historical Venetian city in Crete, source of Malvasia grape vines introduced to Madeira

name: Jardim da Serra
note: Two candidates: n4812192894 is a point in Estreito de Câmara de Lobos parish matching the locality name; n1827635022 is a settlement in Jardim da Serra parish (which is now a separate administrative division of Câmara de Lobos). Both represent the place historically known as Jardim da Serra in the Estreito region.

name: Avenida Manuel de Arriaga
note: The street is now called Avenida Arriaga in OSM. The encyclopedia mentions it as both 'Avenida Manuel de Arriaga' and notes it was formerly 'praça da Constituição'. The modern street matches exactly.

name: Rua da Imperatriz
note: Modern name is 'Rua Imperatriz Dona Amélia' but the encyclopedia refers to it as 'Rua da Imperatriz'. The Wikidata entry confirms the variant 'Rua da Imperatriz D. Amélia' as an alternate name.

name: Avenida João de Deus
note: Modern OSM name is 'Rua de João de Deus' (street rather than avenida), but this is the same feature. The encyclopedia calls it 'Avenida de João de Deus'.

name: Avenida Pedro José de Ornelas
note: Main street matching. Modern name is 'Rua Pedro José de Ornelas' but the encyclopedia refers to it as 'Avenida de Pedro José de Ornelas'. The mentions confirm this is in Santa Luzia parish.

name: Torreão
note: The Torreão is referenced as a locality in Funchal where water infrastructure and sugar factories existed. Multiple OSM features cluster around the Torreão area in São Pedro parish: Adegas do Torreão, Ponte do Torreão, and Edifício Torreão all mark this location.

name: Fonte do Colégio
note: The 'Fonte do Colégio' (fountain at the College) is not directly mapped, but the Colégio dos Jesuítas and Igreja de São João Evangelista (the Jesuit College church) are well-documented features in São Pedro parish that mark this location. The fountain would have been associated with this institution.

name: Capela da Morgada
note: The Capela da Morgada is described as a chapel within the parish church of Porto Santo, with characteristic Manueline architecture. It is not separately mapped in OSM as a distinct structure. The area was in central Funchal (Sé parish based on proximity to cathedral and colégio), but no mapped feature preserves this name.

The encyclopedia mentions 'Ponta das Agulhas' (plural) as one of the major coastal salient points of the Desertas group, specifically at the southern extreme of Bugio. The minor spelling difference (singular vs. plural) is typical of orthographic variation; the location and context match exactly.

name: Estação Semafórica do Ilhéu
note: The text mentions an employee of the semaphore station of 'Ilhéu' in Funchal who worked there for many years. While there are multiple settlements named 'Ilhéu' in OSM (in Machico, Câmara de Lobos, and as islets in the Desertas), and mentions of various 'Estação' features in Funchal, none clearly identify a semaphore station structure. The candidates are either too distant geographically (Estação de Machico), have generic names unrelated to semaphore function, or refer to other Ilhéu locations. Without a precise OSM feature mapping to this historical semaphore station, location remains Funchal municipality only.

name: Rato

name: Porto da Vila do Porto Santo

The OSM settlement 'Vila Baleira Porto Santo' and Geonames 'Vila Baleira' serve as proxies for the location of the port (the modern village name), though they do not precisely identify the quay structure itself.

name: Porto dos Barreiros

While the name differs slightly ('Barbeiros' vs. 'Barreiros'), this is a known spelling variant in historical Portuguese. The OSM stream 'Ribeiro dos Barbeiros' also confirms the location. The feature marks a low/shoal rather than a named port structure, making it a proxy for the port location.

name: Porto das Cagarras
note: OSM node 9123380775 'Porto das Cagarras' is directly matched: it is explicitly named as a bay at Porto Santo island, positioned at the correct bearing (east-northeast) relative to the main village as described in the encyclopedia text.

name: Porto Novo
note: The IRIG entry 'Porto Novo' (settlement) in Porto Santo is the correct match. It is explicitly listed in the enumeration of small ports around Porto Santo island at the southwest bearing as described in the encyclopedia. The modern Porto Santo reference source confirms its location on Porto Santo island.

name: Rocha do Pescador

The OSM 'Rua do Pescador' street serves as a proxy for the location in the village. The feature is a rock/low rather than a named port proper.

name: Ilhéu Redondo

No Porto Santo-specific islet feature in OSM matches the name or context. The feature exists on Porto Santo island but is not mapped in available sources.

name: Baixa da Galé
